models_evaluated: UCLA Health homegrown AI risk model

links.outcome: Potentially preventable hospital admissions after AI-identified care management, stepped-wedge design
links.effect: Potentially preventable HAs dropped 27% (95% CI -44% to -6%); preventable ED visits showed no significant level drop; all HAs -19% (P=.06); all ED visits -15% (P=.06).
links.quote: In the pooled analysis of high-risk and highest-risk patients (n = 3007), potentially preventable HAs showed a statistically significant level drop (-27% [95% CI, -44% to -6%]), without any corresponding change in trends.

links.outcome: Preventable admissions after proactive care management outreach to AI-identified high-risk patients
links.effect: Care management for AI-identified at-risk patients was followed by a 27% significant drop in potentially preventable hospital admissions (95% CI -44% to -6%).
links.quote: A care management intervention targeting AI-identified at-risk patients was followed by a onetime, significant, sizable reduction in preventable HA rates.

screen.reason: The study evaluates a stepped-wedge cluster randomized trial of a proactive care management deployment intervention driven by an AI risk model across 48 primary care clinics.

primary.practice: proactive care management outreach based on AI risk identification
